rationale: Add one aperiodic (1/f) exponent per channel and condition. It is the slope of log-PSD against log-frequency, fitted over 2–7 Hz and 14–40 Hz. Leaving out the alpha band, 50 Hz line noise and the gamma muscle range keeps oscillatory peaks and artifacts out of the fit. MDD has been linked to a shifted excitation/inhibition balance, which shows up in the aperiodic exponent. Relative band power mixes that background slope with the oscillations, and the exponent doesn't depend on amplitude scale, which should help on the external dataset.

The recordings have no artifact rejection, so eye blinks, movement and electrode pops land in a few 2-s Welch segments and inflate their power, mostly in delta and broadband. That adds variance unrelated to the diagnosis. I switch Welch from mean to median averaging across segments (scipy applies the bias correction), which is a cheap way to reject transient artifacts in each subject's power spectrum. It should also help on external datasets with different amounts of artifact. Everything else stays the same.

Nothing else changes.

I'm re-referencing every recording to the common average before computing the PSD. Right now each channel's relative band power depends on the original recording reference. That reference differs between TDBRAIN and the external Mumtaz clinic, and it smears activity from the reference site (for example the mastoids) into every channel. An average reference should give cleaner per-channel spectra that transfer better between amplifiers and clinics. The other features and the classifier are unchanged.

It is fitted on 2–40 Hz, leaving out the alpha peak (7–14 Hz) and the line-noise region, so it adds information the relative band powers don't already capture.
